project.title: Distinct Comammox Nitrospira in a high-rate down-flow hanging sponge reactor treating domestic sewage
project.description: A down-flow hanging sponge (DHS) reactor is a trickling filter-type wastewater treatment system that uses sponges as biomass-retaining carriers. Sponges can promote complete ammonia oxidation (comammox) to nitrate. This study assesses the performance of a compact package-type DHS combined with a sedimentation tank with seven phases at varying hydraulic retention times (HRT). In Phase 7, the BOD of the DHS effluent was maintained at 4.0 +/- 0.5 mgL-1 for the shortest HRT 0.3+/-0.1 h with a low sponge media carrier height (2 m). The nitrification efficiency was considerably impacted by the reduced HRT, with ammonia and nitrate concentrations of 9.0+/-1.2 mgNL-1 and 2.2 +/- 0.5 mgNL-1, respectively. Nevertheless, the effluent met the Thai effluent discharge standard for the duration of the trial. The number of commamox 16S rRNA gene copies ranged from 5.03 to 13.2 x 107 copies mL-1, indicating that comammox could contribute to nitrification in the high-rate DHS reactor.
